## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Add test/support/channels/integration/drivers/whatsapp.ex and test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/whatsapp_test.exs; register Drivers.WhatsApp. Reuse WhatsAppFlowAdapter and WhatsAppFlowTransport in test/support/whatsapp.ex. Extend only that test helper for opt-in response scripting, bounded observations or connector/profile isolation when necessary; preserve all old defaults and callers.
start/1 starts the existing fake external service under ExUnit supervision and supplies linked-device provider registration using WhatsAppFlowAdapter. connect/2 uses the real JidoChatBridge runtime and saved connector/profile, real pairing/storage callback flow and fake scan mechanics from linked_device/integration_flows_test.exs. Headless setup can call the same public pairing/runtime operations; do not add or rewrite UI tests. Observe QR/readiness through existing synchronous/event boundaries.
Emit raw WhatsApp messages through WhatsAppFlowTransport.incoming/2 so the real ConnectionWorker/Message parsing and from_listener path run. Messages include source id, from_jid/channel JID, timestamp, self/history flags and mention JIDs. Direct PN/LID and group @g.us examples must match actual normalization.
Outgoing create/edit/typing uses the current wrapper -> real Adapter -> WhatsAppFlowTransport path. Saved connector resolution stays real and unchanged. Extend script behaviour for matching terminal send/edit failure only through test support, and record all attempts plus resulting recipient mailbox state. The fake is currently globally named, so these tests stay async: false; use unique profiles and clean up only owned profile agents/mailbox entries. Do not pretend the helper is async-safe.
No lib/zaq/channels/bridge.ex, JidoChatBridge, dependencies, Amarula or mix.lock changes. Do not build a WhatsApp WebSocket/Noise emulator. Do not inject a replacement NodeRouter, pipeline, account resolver or history writer.

## Tests to add before implementation
- Existing wrapper continues delegating real transform/send/edit/typing behaviour.
- Fake pairing starts/restores through production storage callbacks and yields a ready connector.
- Direct message and group mention reach the actual agent and correct fake recipient.
- Self/history suppression matches current production contract and does not create extra executions.
- Native author/room JIDs and mention identity survive normalization; profile scopes cannot cross-deliver.
- Controlled terminal send/edit failure, unconfigured request errors and successful mailbox edits.
- Preserve linked_device/integration_flows_test.exs, linked_device/runtime_contracts_test.exs, whatsapp_markdown_delivery_test.exs and existing whatsapp_onboarding_test.exs behaviour. Running existing UI tests is permitted; authoring new UI journeys is outside scope.

## Branches/paths validated
Pairing/restored connection, DM/group mention/passive input, self/history, profile-scoped sends, create/edit/typing, transport success/error and cleanup with a shared singleton.

## Mocking plan
Only WhatsAppFlowTransport and the existing LLM HTTP mock. WhatsAppFlowAdapter is a delegating test wrapper, not reimplemented parsing/routing. The sender/recipient simulation uses the existing supported transport boundary.

## Documentation
Explain this existing wrapper seam, the reason no production transport injection is required, profile ownership, and actual thread/reply capability limits in driver docs and test README.

## Action reuse assessment
Reuse the existing fake/adapter wrappers and production linked-device lifecycle operations. Additive fake scripting is an extension of test infrastructure with unchanged legacy defaults; no new business Action. Inputs/outputs are native messages and transport replies; credentials use synthetic fixture values and real storage callbacks, not copied secrets.

## Done when
WhatsApp passes driver conformance and its real direct/shared paths, has controllable terminal failures and deterministic cleanup, and existing helper consumers retain their expected behaviour.

comments.text: Implemented WhatsApp driver using the existing delegating wrapper, headless real storage-backed pairing, native messages/quotes, opt-in profile-scoped attempt scripting, mailbox edits, self/history suppression and two-profile isolation. Existing helper defaults/assertions unchanged. Validation: linked-device flows/runtime contracts/Markdown regression run 51 tests passing; added profile/history plus existing onboarding run 7 tests passing; complete integration/generator run has only the three separately tracked Telegram failures. mix q passes. No production modules or dependencies changed.

title: [zaq-o9d.5] Implement WhatsApp driver by reusing the existing delegating adapter and fake transport
